role.altitude: The fundraising manager keeps choosing strategy, segments and events, negotiating with suppliers and running the day; building analyses, trackers, registration lists and letters by hand shrinks.
skills_to_grow: Keeping appeal and campaign codes clean so dashboards and plans can trust them
role.ambitious_version: A manager who checks results per donor segment every month and adjusts asks during the year instead of at the yearly plan.

tasks.short: Analyse giving data, look at past results and other charities' approaches, work up ideas with the team, model income options, write the strategy, get it approved and put the targets in place.

steps.what: Fundraising manager pulls giving history, retention, average gift and lapsed donors per segment from the donor CRM into a spreadsheet
Fundraising manager reads sector reports, past campaign reviews and what other charities do
Fundraising manager develops strategies to encourage new or increased contributions with the fundraising team and the director
Fundraising manager models expected income per option from donor numbers, retention and average gift
Fundraising manager writes the strategy: segments, asks, channels, targets and the reasons for them

loop.input: The manager's list of decided points per segment, the income projection table and the strategy template.
loop.output: Draft strategy sections with the figures placed in tables.
loop.check: Every figure must match a cell in the income projection or the giving dashboard dataset, or it is marked; points not on the manager's list are removed; the manager edits every section.
loop.stop: One draft per version of the decided points; if rejected, the manager writes the section.
loop.why_not_simpler: The template holds headings and tables, not the reasoning for each segment.

steps.what: Executive director reviews the final strategy and approves it
Fundraising manager sets the approved targets per segment in the CRM and briefs the team

approvals.approved_version: fundraising strategy, final version approved in s6; any change to targets or segments voids it

tasks.design: A giving dashboard on the donor {CRM} shows retention, upgrades, lapsed donors and average gift per segment and appeal code, so the manager reads results instead of building them. A projection sheet multiplies donor numbers, retention and average gift per option, with the manager's assumptions in one place. A bounded step drafts strategy sections from the manager's decided points with every figure checked against the projection; ideas, choices and the team briefing stay with the manager, and the director approves the final version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Gift data had to be exported and pivoted by hand each time, so analysis was done once a year.
tasks.enabler_now: Donor CRMs report by segment and appeal code; language models draft text whose figures can be checked against a table.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing what will make a donor give more; the data shows what happened, not why.
tasks.human_edge: Judging which ask fits which donor group and getting the team behind it.

ambition.what: Check retention and upgrades per segment every month and adjust asks during the year.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends strategy time on choices and the team instead of on exports; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether a segment dashboard read monthly changes decisions or only reports them.

evidence.claim: Donor CRMs report giving, retention and lapsed donors by segment and appeal code.
Language models can draft sections from listed points, and each figure can be checked against a table.
Segmenting donors for asks is direct marketing; a donor's objection, including to profiling, stops it.

assumptions: Boundary: from the giving analysis to targets set and the team briefed; running the campaigns is outside.

Input contract for s1: gift records in the {CRM} with donor id, date, amount, channel and appeal code; producer is gift entry by the database officer and the payment provider import; fallback is a manual export.
Coverage: about 80% of gifts carry a usable appeal code; the s1 saving is priced at that share and the rest is traced by hand.
Donors who objected to direct marketing are excluded from segments by a CRM flag.
Team ideas, reading outside material, the director's review and the briefing do not change.
unknowns: How clean appeal codes are in the donor CRM.
How often the strategy is refreshed.
research_questions: Does a monthly segment view change any asks during the year?
How much of the drafted strategy text is kept?

already_counted.description: Fundraising manager reads the giving dashboard and traces uncoded gifts.
Fundraising manager sets projection assumptions and checks the results.
Fundraising manager edits drafted strategy sections and fixes marked figures.

incremental.description: Fundraising manager keeps segment and appeal-code definitions in the dashboard current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small donor base with poor appeal coding, so many gifts are still traced by hand; high: a CRM with clean appeal codes and a yearly strategy refresh with several options to model.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Draft the yearly fundraising budget, get it approved and loaded, approve spend against it, track actual income and costs, investigate differences and report monthly.

steps.what: Fundraising manager drafts the yearly budget per campaign and event from last year's actuals in a spreadsheet
Finance director reviews the final budget file and approves it
Finance team keys the approved budget into the ERP per cost centre and campaign code
Fundraising manager approves purchase requests and invoices for events, printing and agencies after checking the remaining budget
Fundraising manager exports costs from the ERP and income from the CRM each month and updates the budget tracker
Fundraising manager investigates differences and wrong codings with the finance team
Fundraising manager writes the monthly budget report with commentary for the director

loop.input: The month's budget-against-actual table per campaign and the manager's notes on explained differences.
loop.output: Draft commentary per campaign with the main differences and their explanations.
loop.check: Every figure must match a cell in the budget-against-actual dataset, or it is marked; every explanation must come from the manager's notes; the manager edits before sending.
loop.stop: One draft per month; if rejected, the manager writes the commentary.
loop.why_not_simpler: The dashboard shows the numbers; the director wants the reasons in a few sentences.

approvals.approved_version: budget file, final version approved in s2; the import loads that file unchanged and any edit voids it

tasks.design: A budget template prefilled with last year's actuals per campaign code from the {ERP} replaces copying them by hand; after the finance director approves the final file, it is imported into the ledger unchanged. The approval screen in the {PROCUREMENT} system shows the remaining budget for the campaign, and a dashboard in {BI} joins ledger costs and {CRM} gifts per campaign code into budget against actual each month. A bounded step drafts the monthly commentary from that table and the manager's notes; investigating differences stays with the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs sat in the ledger and income in the donor CRM, joined each month by exports into a spreadsheet tracker.
tasks.enabler_now: BI tools join ledger and CRM data by a shared campaign code; budget imports run from an approved file.
tasks.still_hard: Gifts and invoices coded to the wrong campaign, and income timing that does not follow the calendar.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding where to cut or add spend when a campaign runs behind.
tasks.altitude: The manager stops building the tracker and spends the time on differences; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether a joined ledger and CRM view removes the monthly reconciliation questions.

evidence.claim: BI tools can join ledger postings and CRM gifts on a shared campaign code to show budget against actual.
Charities often report fundraising costs against income to a regulator or seal body; the rules are national.

assumptions: Boundary: from drafting the yearly budget to the monthly report; mid-year reallocations follow finance's own budget change process and are outside.

Input contract for s5: ledger postings with cost centre and campaign code, produced by the accounts payable team from the manager's coded approvals in s4; gift records with appeal code mapped to campaign code, produced by gift entry and the payment provider import; fallback is the monthly export.
Coverage: about 85% of postings and gifts carry a campaign code; the s5 saving is priced at that share and uncoded items are traced by hand.
The finance director's review and the investigation of differences do not change; finance's time is outside the manager's savings.
unknowns: Whether CRM income is reconciled to the ledger each month by finance.
Number of campaigns and events with their own code.
research_questions: How many differences are wrong codings rather than real overspend?
How much of the drafted commentary does the director read?

already_counted.description: Fundraising manager adjusts the prefilled budget figures.
Fundraising manager reads the budget dashboard and traces uncoded items.
Fundraising manager edits the drafted commentary.

incremental.description: Fundraising manager maps new campaigns and appeal codes in the dashboard.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many invoices and gifts without a campaign code, so part of the tracker survives; high: all postings and gifts coded and the dashboard used every month.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review past campaign results, pick target segments, plan activities with volumes, costs and expected income, get quotes, discuss with colleagues, get approval and set up the campaigns.

steps.what: Fundraising manager reviews past campaign results: response rate, average gift and cost per euro raised per channel
Fundraising manager selects target segments in the CRM and counts donors per segment, leaving out those who objected or have no consent for the channel
Fundraising manager drafts the activity plan: calendar, channels, asks, volumes, costs and expected income
Fundraising manager asks printers, mailing houses and venues for quotes and puts the costs in the plan
Fundraising manager discusses the plan with the team, communications and finance and settles the final version
Executive director reviews the final activity plan and approves it
Fundraising manager creates the campaign records in the CRM and the tasks on the project board

approvals.approved_version: final activity plan table as approved in s6; the import reads that version unchanged and any edit voids it

tasks.design: A campaign results dashboard joins {CRM} gifts by appeal code with {ERP} costs, so response, average gift and cost per euro raised per channel are read, not rebuilt. Saved segment queries in the {CRM} count donors and leave out objections and missing consent; a plan template multiplies segment counts by past response and average gift to show expected income and cost per activity. Choosing activities, quotes and the talks with colleagues stay with the manager; after the director approves the final plan, its rows create the campaign records and project tasks by import.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results per channel had to be rebuilt from two systems for every plan, and segment counts were done by ad hoc exports.
tasks.enabler_now: CRM saved queries with consent flags and BI joins on appeal codes are standard configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Predicting response for a new channel or ask with no history.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing which activities to try and which to drop when the history is thin.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends planning time on choices and supplier talks; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether planned income from past response is close enough to use as a target.

evidence.claim: CRMs keep saved segment queries that respect consent and objection flags.
Marketing e-mail needs prior consent, except to own supporters for similar offers with an opt-out each time.
An objection to direct marketing, including profiling, stops it.

assumptions: Boundary: from past results to campaigns set up; running and sending the campaigns are outside.
Input contract for s1: gift records with appeal code from gift entry and the payment provider import; ledger postings with campaign code from accounts payable; fallback is exports.
Input contract for s2: consent per channel and objection flags in the {CRM}, kept by the database officer from sign-up forms and opt-out requests.
Coverage: about 80% of past campaigns carry clean appeal and campaign codes; s1 is priced at that share.
Quotes, the talks with colleagues and the director's review do not change.
unknowns: How many activities a yearly plan holds.
Whether costs are coded per campaign in the ledger.
research_questions: How far is planned income from actual income per activity?
How often does the plan change after quotes come in?

already_counted.description: Fundraising manager reads the results dashboard and traces uncoded campaigns.
Fundraising manager sets response assumptions per activity and checks the plan figures.

incremental.description: Fundraising manager keeps saved segment queries and plan template assumptions current.
Fundraising manager maps new appeal codes in the results dashboard.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a plan with mostly new channels and poor past coding, so results are rebuilt by hand; high: a yearly plan repeating known appeals with clean codes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set the event concept and budget, book suppliers, organise volunteers, handle registrations and confirmations, collect auction lots and the catalogue, run the day, record income and costs, and thank everyone.

steps.what: Fundraising manager sets the event concept, income target and budget
Fundraising manager books the venue, caterer and other suppliers and agrees terms
Volunteers reply by e-mail with the shifts they can do
Fundraising manager builds the volunteer shift schedule and sends briefings and reminders
Participants register by e-mail or phone and pay by bank transfer
Fundraising manager records registrations in a spreadsheet and matches bank transfers to them
Fundraising manager writes the confirmation e-mail for participants
Fundraising manager sends each paid participant the confirmation
Businesses and supporters send details of donated auction lots by e-mail
Fundraising manager writes lot descriptions and lays out the auction catalogue

loop.input: The lot details form per lot: item, donor name, stated value, conditions of use.
loop.output: A short description per lot, placed with the lot fields in the catalogue template.
loop.check: Every item name, value, date and donor name in the text must match the form fields, or the description is marked; the manager edits each description.
loop.stop: One draft per lot; if rejected, the manager writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: The template places the fields but does not write the sentence that makes a lot attractive.

steps.what: Fundraising manager proofreads the final catalogue and sends it to the printer
Fundraising manager directs the event on the day: programme, volunteers, suppliers and guests
Volunteers write winning bids on the bid sheets and count cash donations
Fundraising manager records actual income per stream and costs and reconciles them with bank and invoices
Fundraising manager writes thank-you letters to participants, donors and lot donors with what they gave or raised
Fundraising manager e-mails or posts the thank-you letters

approvals.approved_version: confirmation text for this event as approved in s7; each mail merges only name and registration details, and any text change voids it
merged thank-you batch (letter text, recipient list and amounts from the event results) as approved in s15 after the merge; any change voids it

tasks.design: A sign-up form in the {WORKFLOW} platform fills the volunteer shift schedule, and an event registration form with online payment writes participants to the {CRM} and marks them paid, so the manager handles exceptions instead of matching transfers. Confirmations go to paid participants from a text the manager approves per event; lot donors fill a lot form, and a bounded step drafts each lot description, checked against the form, for the manager to edit. After the event, registration income comes from the payment records and costs from coded {ERP} invoices; the manager types the winning bids from the signed bid sheets and the cash count, and thank-you letters are merged from those actual results and sent after the manager approves the batch.
tasks.previous_blocker: Registrations, payments, volunteer shifts and lots lived in separate spreadsheets and mail threads that had to be matched by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Event registration with online payment and sign-up forms are standard configuration; language models draft short descriptions checked against form fields.
tasks.still_hard: Suppliers, volunteers and the day itself; most event work is people and logistics.
tasks.human_edge: Running the day so that guests give more than they planned.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time on lists and matching and more on suppliers, volunteers and guests; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Which share of participants still registers by phone or e-mail once a form exists.

evidence.claim: An event module replaced Excel for one company's customer event; 460 customers registered for it (vendor case, no time figures).
Registration forms with online payment can write participants to a CRM and mark them paid.
Participants' details collected for an event may be used for later appeals only with consent or an opt-out offered each time.

assumptions: Boundary: from the event concept to thank-yous sent; supplier invoices and payment run through purchasing and finance.

Input contract for s6: registration form fields name, e-mail, event option and amount, written to the {CRM} with the payment provider's paid status; producer is the participant (s5); fallback is the manager typing phone and e-mail registrations.
Coverage: about 70% of participants register and pay online; the s6 saving is priced at that share.
Self-service: participants, volunteers and lot donors fill forms with about the effort of today's e-mails; that time is shown in s3, s5 and s9 and is outside the manager's savings.
Event results are actual values: payments received, winning bids from the signed bid sheets and the counted cash, not ticket targets or lot estimates.
Supplier bookings, proofreading the catalogue and the day itself do not change.
unknowns: How many events per year and of which type.
Share of income from tickets, auction and donations on the day.
research_questions: How many registrations still need manual matching after online payment?
Do drafted lot descriptions change bid levels?

already_counted.description: Fundraising manager places volunteers the sign-up form could not fit and fixes clashes.
Fundraising manager handles phone registrations and failed payments.
Fundraising manager edits drafted lot descriptions.
Fundraising manager types winning bids and cash counts and checks the results.
Fundraising manager reviews the merged thank-you batch.

incremental.description: Fundraising manager sets up the registration, sign-up and lot forms for each event.
Fundraising manager keeps the letter and catalogue templates current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a sponsored walk with paper sign-ups and mostly cash on the day; high: a ticketed gala with online registration, an auction catalogue and many thank-yous.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
